records.text: Nalesette Wildbringer is a pet trainer in Felwood who helps hunters and their pets. Nalesette describes training as something hunters can pass on to their companions and addresses visitors as friends.
Malygen is a general-goods vendor whose shop offers goods for customers to browse.
Bale is a general-goods vendor who offers goods for customers to browse.

Kaerbrus is a hunter trainer who offers training and information about dual talent specialization. His greetings vary by character: one welcomes the visitor to the Cenarion Circle, while another says he cannot train that character.
Vile Ooze is a solitary-looking ooze found across several parts of Feralas, including the Woodpaw Hills and Ruins of Isildien.
Ironbeak Owls are found in several parts of Feralas, including the High Wilderness and the Ruins of Isildien.
Ironbeak Screechers are found in parts of Feralas, including the High Wilderness and the Ruins of Isildien.
Ironbeak Hunters range across several parts of Feralas, from the Woodpaw Hills and Ruins of Isildien to the High Wilderness.
Warpwood Moss Flayers are found in the High Wilderness of Feralas.
Warpwood Shredders are found in the High Wilderness and elsewhere in Feralas. They use Thrash while fighting.
Dessecus is a powerful demon in Felwood.
A Jadefire satyr dwelling in Felwood, among the satyrs that spread corruption through the land. Eridan Bluewind describes them as led by the cruel Xavathras and gathered at the Ruins of Constellas.
A Jadefire satyr rogue counted among the minions spreading corruption in Felwood. Eridan Bluewind names the rogues alongside Xavathras’s other followers.

A Jadefire satyr trickster in Felwood’s northern encampment. Eridan Bluewind says the encampment’s tricksters and betrayers feed on the corruption of native creatures, as part of a wider plan involving a corrupted moonwell.
A Jadefire felsworn counted among the minions spreading corruption around Felwood. Eridan Bluewind names the felsworns among Xavathras’s followers at the Ruins of Constellas.
A Jadefire shadowstalker counted among the minions spreading corruption around Felwood. Eridan Bluewind names the shadowstalkers among Xavathras’s followers at the Ruins of Constellas.

A Jadefire Hellcaller is one of the satyrs serving in the northern Felwood corruption around Xavaric. Eridan Bluewind identifies Hellcallers among the forces to defeat as they threaten the land and feed on its corruption.

A Jaedenar Cultist belongs to the cultist forces inhabiting the corrupted barrow dens of Jaedenar. Greta Mosshoof identifies the Jaedenar group as part of the Shadow Council, which plots there with the Burning Legion; she asks travelers to prove their opposition by fighting its members.

A Jaedenar Guardian serves among the forces inhabiting Jaedenar’s corrupted barrow dens. Greta Mosshoof identifies these Jaedenar forces with the Shadow Council’s plots alongside the Burning Legion, and asks travelers to fight them to demonstrate opposition to the council.
A Jaedenar Enforcer is one of the hostile Jaedenar figures found across areas of Felwood.

A Jaedenar Adept belongs to the forces inhabiting the corrupted barrow dens of Jaedenar. Greta Mosshoof associates the Jaedenar forces with the Shadow Council, which plots with the Burning Legion, and asks travelers to oppose the council by fighting its members.
A Jaedenar Darkweaver is a hostile figure found around Jaedenar and nearby Felwood areas.
A Jaedenar warlock who summons an imp outside combat and uses shadow magic in battle. When badly wounded, it may flee to call for aid.
A Jaedenar hound found in the corrupted barrow dens. It is one of the beasts Greta Mosshoof asks the player to slay as proof of opposition to the Shadow Council.
A Jaedenar hunter found around Jaedenar in Felwood. Its name and presence place it among the area’s hunting forces.
A Toxic Horror inhabiting a part of Jaedenar. In combat it casts a toxic attack.
An Infernal Sentry encountered in Jaedenar. It reacts to being engaged by casting a spell.
Immolatus is a powerful, singular presence in Jaedenar who uses a combat spell.
An Irontree creature encountered in Felwood. It casts a spell when badly wounded.
An Irontree creature encountered in Felwood. It casts a spell while fighting.
A Withered Protector in Felwood that can become enraged and cast a spell in combat.
A member of the corrupted Deadwood tribe in Felwood, identified by Grazle as one of the warriors his people want driven back.
A member of the corrupted Deadwood tribe in Felwood. In combat it can spread the Curse of the Deadwood, and it can use Rejuvenation.
A member of the corrupted Deadwood tribe in Felwood, identified by Grazle as one of the pathfinders his people want driven back.
The Deadwood Den Watcher is one of the Deadwood furbolgs Nafien identifies as part of the corrupted camp in Felwood, which he asks the player to fight. In combat, it casts Curse of the Deadwood.

The Deadwood Avenger is one of the Deadwood furbolgs Nafien identifies as part of the corrupted camp in Felwood, which he asks the player to fight. It casts Curse of the Deadwood in combat and has an enrage emote.
The Deadwood Shaman is one of the Deadwood furbolgs Nafien identifies as part of the corrupted camp in Felwood, which he asks the player to fight.
Felpaw Wolves are wild creatures found in Felwood. They roam the region’s forested areas and defend themselves with a combat spell.
Felpaw Scavengers are creatures found in Felwood.
Felpaw Ravagers are creatures of Felwood. Talo Thornhoof’s hunting request names them among the beasts adventurers are asked to kill there; they defend themselves with Thrash.

Eridan is an Emerald Circle member working to heal Felwood's corruption. He senses the suffering of the ancient ones and helps cleanse evil from artifacts. He also directs efforts against the Jadefire satyrs, whom he describes as spreading corruption under their cruel leader, Xavathras.

In Eridan Bluewind's account, Xavathras is the cruel leader of the Jadefire satyrs at the Ruins of Constellas, who spread Felwood's corruption. Xavathras and his followers are part of a wider effort to cultivate a corrupted moonwell and provide its spoils to Xavaric.
Chieftain Bloodmaw is an individually named combatant.
Dreka’Sur recounts that her husband said a druid had asked him to fight the furbolg Overlord Ror; neither man was heard from again. Seeking revenge for being left a widow, she wants Ror’s claw.

Golhine the Hooded is a druid trainer in Felwood. He describes tranquility as something a druid can find even within cold stone walls, by looking inward. He speaks of a later calling from the Emerald Dream, where a druid will hibernate and continue training among pure forms.

Lord Banehollow is an imperious demon in Jaedenar who guards his authority from Lord Hel'nurath and his servant Ulathek, whom he calls a spy. He demands proof of loyalty through Ulathek's death, then grants the petitioner slightly more patience. He will also let a seeker obtain Xorothian stardust from his servant Ur'dan, provided they can pay.

Shadow Lord Fel'dan is the mortal leader in Shadow Hold, making pacts with the Legion and directing the threat against Felwood. Greta Mosshoof identifies him as the head of the serpent and names two succubi as his servants.
Rakaiah is a succubus in Shadow Hold and the torturer of Trey Lightforge. Her role in Trey's death is one of the loose ends Arko'narin's allies seek to resolve while she mourns.

Arathandris Silversky is an Emerald Circle druid working to reclaim Felwood from corruption. She studies corrupted life, including sap from Warpwood elementals she considers beyond cleansing, in hopes of saving other forms of life. She shares cleansing knowledge only with people she knows and trusts. Her work also includes purifying fel creep and tainted mining vitriol into reagents for Cenarion plant salve; a Cenarion beacon helps gatherers identify corrupted materials.

Maybess Riverbreeze is an Emerald Circle druid working to restore Felwood's corrupted plant life. She studies the tainted sap of irredeemably corrupted Warpwood elementals and knows how to purify corrupted herbs and mining byproducts into reagents for Cenarion plant salve. She asks would-be helpers to prove their commitment to the Cenarion Circle before sharing her cleansing knowledge.

Arei is an ancient spirit trapped in corrupted Felwood, still suffering with the land. She asks for help reaching safety and rest, and says fighting her own kind deeply saddens her. As her spirit recovers, she feels the forest's hold loosening and says she can finally be at peace; she directs her helper to seek Kayneth Stillwind in Forest Song.

Dreka'Sur is a widow at Bloodvenom Post who seeks vengeance for her husband's death in Felwood. After he vanished while helping a druid against Overlord Ror, she asks for the furbolg's claw as payment for what it did to her family. Even after learning her husband died in battle, she says she could not rest until Ror paid for leaving her alone.

Salia is a succubus servant of Shadow Lord Fel'dan in Shadow Hold. Greta Mosshoof identifies her as one of the two servants alongside Moora and names her among the targets of the strike against Fel'dan, who is making pacts with the Legion.

Moora is a succubus servant of Shadow Lord Fel'dan in Shadow Hold. Greta Mosshoof identifies her as one of the two servants alongside Salia and names her among the targets of the strike against Fel'dan, who is making pacts with the Legion.
A Jaedenar Legionnaire is a combatant associated with the Jaedenar area of Felwood.
Prince Xavalis is a named combatant in Jaedenar, Felwood.

An Entropic Beast is an entropic elemental roaming Shatter Scar Vale, among the creatures Taronn Redfeather asks to be sought out while assessing the craters and their corrupt water. It attacks with a spell when engaged.

An entropic elemental roaming the old infernal craters of Shatter Scar Vale. Taronn Redfeather asks travelers to check whether these creatures remain and whether corrupt water still fills the craters.

Winna Hazzard is a Forsaken researcher at Bloodvenom Post who wants to turn corrupted moonwell water into an advantage against the Alliance. She experiments on her kitten, whose size and strength increase after exposure, and asks for a water sample to continue her work. Her enthusiasm for the results is unmistakable.

Trull Failbane coordinates an investigation into the wildkin of Winterspring, which he believes may guard secrets of the night elves. He uses successive hunts to probe the region, including reports of caves where wildkin may be protecting something valuable. His orders are deliberate and demanding, but he recognizes hard work and believes the investigation is making progress.
Altsoba Ragetotem is a weapon merchant. Travelers can browse the goods, and Altsoba also offers repairs.

Xavaric is a satyr leader in northern Felwood, directing an encampment that feeds on the corruption of native creatures. Eridan Bluewind's account links Xavaric's followers to a plan to cultivate a corrupted moonwell and bring its spoils to him. Xavaric is described as cruel.
Winna's Kitten is a kitten belonging to Winna.

Kelek Skykeeper is an Emerald Circle druid working in Felwood, where the Circle seeks to heal the land. His experience studying the Winterfall furbolg makes him a useful interpreter of their crudely written log, though he says little is known about them and promises only to send word after examining it.

Taronn Redfeather, an Emerald Circle druid in Felwood, investigates the corruption still damaging the forest. He wants to know whether Shatter Scar Vale's craters hold corrupt water and whether entropic elementals remain. The water's persistence disappoints him: he hoped for a pure source to aid healing. He fears crossing an infernal, yet plans to save forest creatures and destroy those too corrupted to be safe.

Greta Mosshoof, an Emerald Circle druid in Felwood, first tests whether helpers oppose the Shadow Council. She seeks to learn its leadership through scrying, arranging for her old friend, the shaman Islen Waterseer, to help purify water that can quench the Council's protective braziers. Greta identifies Shadow Lord Fel'dan as the mortal making pacts with the Burning Legion and says a frontal attack is the only way she sees to stop him.
Tenell Leafrunner is an Emerald Circle questgiver in Felwood.

Ivy Leafrunner is an Emerald Circle member occupied with work in Felwood. She describes Winterspring as harsh but rich in ancient elven ruins and places to explore; though she has not had the chance to travel there herself, she directs the traveler to Starfall Village to consult Wynd Nightchaser, whom she says knows the area well.

Arko'narin and her longtime friend Trey Lightforge came to Jaedenar to investigate the Shadow Council, but were captured and separated. Imprisoned and stripped of their equipment, she fears Trey is dead and that the cultists will sacrifice her. She asks for the key to escape, then means to recover their gear and Trey's sword, Lightforge, before reporting to her superiors. Her urgency reflects both the danger at Shadow Hold and her concern for her friend.

Jessir Moonbow came from Darnassus to meet two friends investigating the Shadow Council in Jaedenar; when they were days late, she feared something had happened. After Arko'narin escapes, Jessir says she hurried toward Darnassus with Trey's sword and was too distressed to stop for healing. Jessir understands that Trey, one of Arko'narin's closest friends, has died and is being mourned. She asks for help bringing Trey's torturer to justice and recovering his remains so his friends can honor him.
Della is Jessir's pet, living in Felwood.
The Bloodvenom Post Braves are a named group associated with Bloodvenom Post.
Shi'alune is Kaerbrus' pet, living at Bloodvenom Post.
Timbermaw Warders are found across Felwood, Winterspring, and Moonglade. Their name identifies a warding role.
Timbermaw Mystics are found in Felwood and Winterspring. Their name identifies a mystical role.

Grazle represents the wary Timbermaw in Felwood. He says the uncorrupted tribe has faced hostility from outsiders and trusts few; he asks newcomers to prove themselves by driving back the corrupted Deadwood furbolg. He also offers recognition for Deadwood feathers, while warning that his brethren may still need convincing.

Gorn One Eye is a distrustful Timbermaw in Timbermaw Hold. He tells visitors that earning the trust of a few does not prove themselves to him. He also seeks the demon Xandivious's essence as part of healing the Winterfall tribe, and sends a Timbermaw peace offering to the Alliance or Horde leader according to the visitor's people.

Meilosh is a Timbermaw furbolg whose dealings in cloth reflect his people’s guarded outlook and distinct traditions. He explains that Timbermaw are content among themselves and wary of strangers, while runecloth offers a rare opportunity for trade. Mooncloth, by contrast, is sacred to his people; he offers to teach a fashioning technique in exchange for it. He also considers training an ally who proves trustworthy.

Kernda is a Timbermaw furbolg who examines ritual objects brought from the Deadwood and Winterfall. She recognizes the Deadwood totem’s decay and judges the Winterfall totem twisted by an incomprehensible force, seeing both as signs of the corruption afflicting those tribes. Kernda hopes study and ritual may reveal what has turned their brethren against them, and receives the totems for that investigation from those permitted to speak with the Timbermaw.
Brakkar is a wind rider master who offers fast travel. When attacked, he calls for guards and summons an enraged wyvern.
Mishellena is a hippogryph master who offers air travel and quest services. If attacked, she calls for guards.
Death Howl is a rare beast found in Felwood, known for its silvery claws.
Alshirr Banebreath is a named combatant who casts a spell while fighting.
Ragepaw is a humanoid who casts spells when it draws aggression and during combat.
Olm the Wise is a beast who casts a spell during combat.
Mongress is a beast that can become enraged.
The Ongar is a creature in Felwood. It can cast a spell in combat.

Kroshius is an infernal whom Niby describes as fallen and nearly burned out. Niby’s task calls for reigniting his remains; after being summoned, Kroshius cries, “Kroshius live? Kroshius crush!” and fights with Knock Away.

Niby the Almighty is a boastful warlock who directs the effort to reanimate the infernal Kroshius. He grandly announces the summoning to his servant Impsy, then reacts to the result with a chicken joke. He rages at being expelled from Stormwind and vows revenge through “Death by chicken,” revealing both his theatrical self-importance and his fixation on proving his power. His exchanges present the infernal ritual as his “greatest conjuration”; he expects Kroshius to be dangerous and tells others to stand clear.

Impsy is Niby’s imp minion, but resents that his master has a pet while he has none. He sets out to make a stuffed one, delighting in felcloth’s painful, evil feel and promising Niby’s belongings as a reward. His banter with Niby is cutting, and he mocks his master’s failures with theatrical deference.
Ur'dan supplies Xorothian stardust from within Shadow Hold in Jaedenar. Banehollow says the supply is his and that it can be bought for a price; Ur'dan’s goods are available to browse.

Ulathek is Banehollow’s servant and spy for the rival dreadlord Hel'nurath, plotting to help him seize power in Jaedenar. When confronted with Banehollow’s message, Ulathek threatens to trap the visitor’s soul in a shard and give it to his imp. He guards his discussions with the dreadlords as private counsel.

Vartrus is one of the Ancients, protectors of the forest. He recounts that their physical forms were destroyed when Archimonde and the Burning Legion marched on Hyjal, but their spirits endured. Concerned about demonic agents corrupting nature, he guides the hunt with inscriptions on his own bark. He offers an Ancient stave to combine with a bowstring Stoma can create.

Stoma the Ancient claims that only he can enchant the bowstring needed for the bow made from Vartrus's stave. He dismisses gathering black dragon sinew as a simple task, calls the seeker “puny one,” and has little patience for idle chatter. He intends to cleanse the sinew of evil before enchanting it into an almost indestructible string.

Hastat calls himself an Ancient of Lore and a keeper of knowledge lost eons ago. He offers to bind one of his leaves with blue dragon sinew into a quiver to accompany a bow of the Ancients. His blessing wishes protection for arrows, true aim, and the downfall of the world's enemies.
Mylini Frostmoon is a weapon merchant. Visitors can browse her goods or request repairs, making her a practical stop for travelers maintaining their arms.

Nafien is a Timbermaw furbolg near the Hold’s entrance in northern Felwood. The corruption afflicting the Deadwood troubles him: he sees them as brethren warped by fel and asks others to stop their threat while sparing him the details. He stresses that Timbermaw trust must be earned and warns that suspicion can make passage through the Hold dangerous. Proof of resistance to corruption can build that trust.

Elder Nightwind is an elder associated with the gathering of the stars. Nightwind speaks of the heavens as holding answers to earthly mysteries, and reads the stars’ changing paths as signs of hope and strength for coming ages. The gathering also directs visitors seeking other named elders.
Gorrim serves as the Emerald Circle’s flight master. When attacked, Gorrim summons an enraged gryphon and wyvern.

place_records.text: You are in Felwood, a corrupted land in Kalimdor where the Alliance and the Horde both hold settlements. Bloodvenom Post belongs to the Horde and Talonbranch Glade to the Alliance, while Emerald Sanctuary is kept by neither side. Corruption breeds tainted oozes and entropic beasts, Angerclaw and Felpaw creatures roam the wilds, and Deadwood furbolgs and Jaedenar cultists are hostile to travelers.
You are in Deadwood Village, a camp of Deadwood furbolgs where corruption permeates the ground. Its warriors, gardeners and pathfinders are hostile, and Overlord Ror is a notable danger here.

You are in Felpaw Village, where Deadwood den watchers, avengers and shamans are hostile. Chieftain Bloodmaw is a notable hostile here, and a strange gooey substance from a cauldron is being studied for its corruption.

You are in Jaedenar, a place of Shadow Council cultists. Jaedenar cultists, adepts, guardians and darkweavers are hostile, and tainted oozes and hounds roam here. A captive named Arko'narin is held in Jaedenar, fearing the cultists will sacrifice her.
You are in Bloodvenom River, where tainted and vile oozes gather alongside Jaedenar warlocks, darkweavers and enforcers, all hostile to travelers.
You are in Bloodvenom Falls, where tainted oozes gather and the hostile creatures Ulathek and The Ongar are notable dangers. Jaedenar darkweavers are also found here.

You are in Shatter Scar Vale, a valley of craters where entropic beasts and horrors, infernal sentries and tainted oozes are hostile. Niby the Almighty, a boastful warlock, is trying to reanimate the infernal Kroshius here with his imp, Impsy.

You are in Irontree Woods, where Irontree stompers, Warpwood shredders, toxic horrors and Angerclaw grizzlies are hostile. Ancients named Vartrus, Stoma and Hastat dwell here, guarding the forest against demonic corruption. A spirit healer is found here.

You are in Timbermaw Hold, home of the Timbermaw furbolgs at the northern edge of Felwood. Nafien keeps watch near its entrance, troubled by the Deadwood furbolgs he sees as brethren warped by fel. Timbermaw wardens and mystics will attack travelers they consider hostile.

You are in Bloodvenom Post, a Horde post in Felwood with a wind rider master, a weapon merchant and a general-goods vendor. Dreka'Sur, a widow, seeks vengeance on Overlord Ror for her husband's death, and Winna Hazzard, a Forsaken researcher, is working to turn corrupted moonwell water against the Alliance. Trull Failbane leads an investigation into the wildkin of Winterspring.

You are in Talonbranch Glade, an Alliance settlement in Felwood with trainers of magic and arms, a hippogryph master and a weapon merchant. Golhine the Hooded, a druid trainer, speaks of tranquility as something a druid finds by looking inward. Angerclaw grizzlies and Felpaw ravagers roam the glade's edges.

You are in Morlos'Aran, a place where Emerald Circle druids work in Felwood. Arathandris Silversky studies corrupted life, including sap from Warpwood elementals, in hopes of saving other forms of life. Felpaw wolves and Angerclaw bears are hostile, and a spirit healer is near.

You are in Emerald Sanctuary, a neutral sanctuary in Felwood where Emerald Circle druids work to heal the land's corruption. Eridan Bluewind directs efforts against the Jadefire satyrs, and Kelek Skykeeper studies the Winterfall furbolgs. Gorrim, a flight master, serves here, and Felpaw wolves prowl its edges.
You are in Jadefire Glen, a glen in Felwood. Jadefire satyrs and Jadefire felsworn haunt its hollows, and Alshirr Banebreath is among the dangers here.
You are in the Ruins of Constellas, a set of ruins in Felwood. Cursed oozes, Jadefire shadowstalkers and rogues, and Jadefire felsworn roam the ruins, along with Angerclaw bears and Felpaw wolves.
You are in Jadefire Run, a route through Felwood. Jadefire tricksters and hellcallers prowl it, along with Felpaw scavengers and Angerclaw maulers, and Xavaric is among the dangers here.

You are in Shadow Hold, a cult stronghold in Felwood. Jaedenar darkweavers, warlocks and enforcers prowl its halls, and vile oozes lurk among them. Arko'narin is imprisoned here, fearing the cultists will sacrifice her.
